events.title: Eric Raymond publishes The Cathedral and the Bazaar
events.summary: Eric Raymond's essay The Cathedral and the Bazaar (1997) argued open, distributed development beats closed planning — influencing Netscape's Mozilla release.
events.about: Raymond's 'given enough eyeballs, all bugs are shallow' became open-source folklore. The essay gave executives a narrative for releasing proprietary code — directly preceding the 1998 Mozilla source dump.

narrative.whyChosen: The essay bridged hacker culture and corporate open-source strategy.
narrative.whyImportant: It gave language for why Netscape and others should open their codebases.
narrative.problemSolved: Executives lacked a business case for releasing source code.
